item.title: #3586603: Scope cleanup can leave an item published with an emptied hard-filter scope
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 22 files, +3487/−58 · php +3228/−41 · md +241/−17 · yml +18
  • Diff: d3d7bc4
  • Discussion: #3586603 · 1 contributor · 21 comments

Summary

Scope cleanup no longer leaves an item published with an emptied scope. Before, deleting a role (or language, term, bundle, referenced entity, or uninstalling a module) could remove the last value limiting a context item, so an item limited to the "Reviewer" role was suddenly delivered to every user, with no log or message. Now cleanup unpublishes such an item (state Archived on the ai_context_editorial workflow), saves a new revision explaining which value was removed, logs a warning per item, and shows the acting user one warning with a count and a link to the item list. After deleting roles, languages, terms or bundles, or uninstalling modules, check the context item list for newly unpublished or archived items. Items that stay published: Global items, items that keep at least one value, and items that only lose Context Tags (ranking only). Sites that already ran post-update 0006 on 1.0.0-beta5 or 1.0.0-rc1 do not run it again, so items it emptied earlier stay published and need manual review.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: ai_context.scope_cleanup service gains new constructor arguments (logger, messenger, current user, time, database, notice service); only relevant to code that instantiates it directly.
  • New API: AiContextItem::canUnpublishWithModerationState() (@internal) and a persisted ai_context.scope_cleanup_notice service (@internal) hold cleanup counts for one warning per request.

Technical details

The change is in AiContextScopeCleanupService. When removeScopeValuesFromItems() empties a scope, or removeEntityItemReference() removes the last Specific Entities reference, widensWhenEmptied() decides whether the item would reach more requests. The rule: any stored-value scope except Context Tags (RANKING_ONLY_SCOPES) counts as a hard filter, custom stored-value scopes included, and there is no public policy API in 1.0. Global items are never unpublished. A subcontext item with no stored inherit flag is unpublished when it would resolve to a Global parent, even if the emptied value was a tag.

Unpublishing uses setUnpublishedWithModerationState() on every published translation, saved in one database transaction. publish_on (and publish_state when present) is cleared on every translation so Scheduler cannot republish it. The save is a new revision with a log message, the current user as author, and the request time. Saves that do not unpublish use setSyncing(TRUE) so content moderation does not add a revision that copies the old log message. If a moderated workflow has no unpublished default-revision state (AiContextItem::canUnpublishWithModerationState()), the item is not saved: the stale value stays (it matches no request), an error is logged once per scope, and the warning gets an extra sentence. Already unpublished items get the stale value removed with no revision, log or message, unless they have a publish_on date, in which case it is cancelled in a new revision.

Counts live in the new ai_context.scope_cleanup_notice service, tagged persist so one warning with totals survives the container rebuild during a module uninstall. The messenger warning is skipped for the anonymous user (cron, Drush) and deferred until the surrounding transaction commits on entity delete. Post-update 0006 uses the same rule. Docs for scopes, services and custom scopes were updated, and kernel tests were added including AiContextScopeCleanupForeignValuesTest (one case per trigger) and a new ai_context_test_item_save_fail test module.

Upgrade

Site owners: after drush updatedb (post-update 0006), after deleting roles, languages, terms, vocabularies or bundles, or after module uninstalls, review the context item list for newly unpublished or archived items and re-check their scope before republishing. On sites that already ran 0006 on 1.0.0-beta5 or 1.0.0-rc1, review published items that have no Roles, Languages, Site Sections, Entity Types, Taxonomy Terms or Specific Entities value. Custom workflows need an unpublished state with Published cleared and Default revision selected, or cleanup will not save the item and logs an error. Custom stored-value scope authors: cleanup now treats your scope as a hard filter.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 18, 2026
  • Committed: November 2, 2026 (15 days later)

item.title: #3594867: Gold labeling still serves legacy tool steps whose output is only "assistant:"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +200/−14 · php +194/−13 · md +6/−1
  • Diff: 97e5972
  • Discussion: #3594867 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In ai_eval 1.1.x, traces imported from AI Observability in the legacy text format could show an agent's tool step as a reply of just "assistant:". These steps were wrongly treated as final answers. They appeared on the gold labeling screen and counted toward coverage, agreement and judge validation. They are now excluded. Promoting such a step is refused, and so is promoting an embeddings call, which has no text answer to test. The trace card explains why. "Promote all" now picks the real final answer of an agent run. On the compare page, a difference that reads the same on both sides, such as a changed dataset hash, now shows once ("Dataset content: changed") instead of "A: changed; B: changed". Labels already saved on tool steps stay but are no longer counted.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: TraceBrowser::isRoleLabelOnly(), PromotionService::STATUS_TOOL_STEP and PromotionService::STATUS_NO_ANSWER outcome statuses.

Technical details

TraceBrowser::isFinalAnswer() now also requires that the reply is not role-label-only. The new TraceBrowser::isRoleLabelOnly() trims response_text and strips a leading assistant: (case-insensitive). If nothing is left, the reply is a tool step. GoldSetAgreement and HumanLabelSource inherit the fix through isFinalAnswer().

PromotionService::promotionIntegrityFlag() returns two new flags. no_answer (STATUS_NO_ANSWER) applies when response_kind is set, as for embeddings. tool_step (STATUS_TOOL_STEP) applies when the reply is role-label-only and there are no response_tools. Both count as refused in the promotion report. For agent runs, the "Promote all" selection of the last chat now calls TraceBrowser::isFinalAnswer() instead of its own text and tools check. As a result, a trailing "assistant:" step is skipped and an earlier real answer is chosen.

PromoteFragment gains toolStepNotice() and noAnswerNotice(). TraceReviewFragment renders them as a refusal_notice warning with "This trace cannot be promoted." In ResultsCompareController, the two readable values are compared as strings. When they match, a single value is shown, otherwise the "A: @a; B: @b" form is kept. The user guide and changelog are updated. Existing tests that expected embeddings to promote with an empty answer now expect a refusal.

Upgrade

No update steps are needed. Embeddings calls can no longer be promoted, so any workflow that relied on promoting them with an empty AI response will now see them refused.

item.title: #3620031: Adopt the three-tier protocol: block Restricted images, warn on Moderate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +100/−28 · md +88/−18 · yml +10/−8 · json +2/−2
  • Diff: 2469b0d
  • Discussion: #3620031 · 2 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

The image safety recipe now has three tiers instead of a binary block. Safe images save silently. Moderate images (partial nudity, suggestive content, mild violence) are accepted, and the uploader sees a warning. Restricted images (full nudity, explicit sexual content, gore, graphic violence, graphic medical imagery) are still blocked with a validation error. An image the model cannot classify is treated as Restricted. Sites that already applied the recipe do not pick this up automatically.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal/ai_validations constraint raised from ^1.3 to ^1.4, which provides the opt-in XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK warning tier (#3606131).
  • Config change: Shipped field_validation.rule_set.media_image rule: new title, XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK prompt, reworded message, new warningMessage key in the rule data.

Technical details

The rule's prompt in config/field_validation.rule_set.media_image.yml now returns XSAFE, XWARN or XBLOCK in place of XTRUE/XFALSE. The rule title becomes "Block restricted imagery, warn on moderate". The message text now covers only Restricted content, and the new warningMessage key in the rule's data holds the Moderate text. The rule's provider is unchanged, an empty string meaning the site default. recipe.yml and the composer.json description are reworded, and composer.json requires drupal/ai_validations ^1.4.

The warning tier is opt-in in AI Validations and is active only while the warning message is non-empty. The README says that emptying it returns validation to XTRUE/XFALSE, and that the prompt must then be rewritten to match. If only one of the two is changed, uploads are blocked (empty message with the three-token prompt) or no warning is ever shown (message set with the two-token prompt). The README also documents "Adjusting the tiers", for example mapping Moderate to XBLOCK or XSAFE. It states that an XWARN verdict also writes to the ai_validations logger channel, so headless flows such as JSON:API keep an audit trail and are never blocked by a warning.

Upgrade

The recipe creates the rule set with createIfNotExists, so re-applying the new version on a site that already has the media_image rule set changes nothing. Either delete the rule set at Structure → Field Validation and re-apply the recipe, or edit the existing rule by hand:

=== DECISION ===
- If the image is SAFE, respond with: XSAFE
- If the image is MODERATE, respond with: XWARN
- If the image is RESTRICTED, respond with: XBLOCK

=== OUTPUT FORMAT ===
Respond with exactly one token — XSAFE, XWARN, or XBLOCK — and nothing else.

Then fill in the rule's Warning message field. Update drupal/ai_validations to 1.4 or newer.

  • Committed: November 2, 2026 (2 months later)

item.title: #3594862: Compare page lists raw snapshot keys, sha256 hashes and JSON as the differences
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594862 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

This one commit on 1.1.x covers #3594862 and seven related fixes (#3594855 to #3594861). The compare page now lists differences with plain names such as "Dataset content" or "Judge model". Dataset and rubric hashes show as "changed" or "same", and the raw keys and values sit in a closed "Technical details" section. Grader ids become grader labels, and the heading reads "1 difference" in the singular. Result screens show the gate a run recorded, or "Gate not recorded", rather than a made-up 4.0 threshold, and they show test labels with the id as a tooltip. Hard and soft gate wording now says the type only changes the exit code of drush ai-eval:run. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred", still adding up to 100%. Annotate progress counts labeled answers against the latest run. Calibration screens now warn when a saved fit will not apply because the rubric wording changed, and they say when a save replaced an earlier inactive fit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ResultsCompareController::__construct() gains an optional trailing ?PluginManagerInterface $graderManager argument (wired to ai_eval.grader_manager). FailureRateService rows gain a verdict key.
  • New API: GateTypeWording helper class in Drupal\ai_eval\Form supplies gate type labels and descriptions shared by the target and guided forms.

Technical details

Compare page: ResultsCompareController gets differenceLabel() (a match from snapshot key to translatable label, unknown keys keep the raw key) and readableValue(). readableValue() collapses dataset_sha256 and rubric_sha256 to changed, same, recorded or not recorded, with per-rubric-reference states. It maps metric through GateMetric::label(), gate to Hard or Soft, and grader ids in grader_ids, must_pass, judge_prompt_versions and judge_models to plugin labels from the injected grader manager. Raw values are rendered in a details element (#open FALSE) titled "Technical details". RunComparability is unchanged. The heading uses formatPlural(). When the two runs belong to different tests, the warning uses test labels with the id in a title attribute and adds cache tags.

Gate display: EvalResultsController::recordedGate() builds the GateThreshold from the run's validated snapshot (metric and threshold), then falls back to the live test, then returns NULL. A NULL gate drops the threshold and the gate comparison from the aria label, and the detail page shows "Gate not recorded". Metric names show as labels instead of ids. The overview also loads targets once up front, so tables and the pending-optimization list can show target labels with cache tags. A new GateTypeWording class feeds the options and description in EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm.

Annotation and calibration: FailureRateService::decorate() merges tagged rows by failure mode and splits rows with no failure mode by verdict (pass, fail, defer). Rows now carry a verdict key, and the old "(untagged)" label is gone. WorkflowStateService drops the fixed suggested target of 100. Step 2 progress is canonical annotations on the latest result over its question_count, and the ribbon label is plural-aware ("N of M answers labeled"). CalibrationSaveTrait::saveAndReport() counts inactive earlier curves for the same provider, model and fingerprint before saving, and reports the replacement afterwards. CalibrationFromReviewsForm compares the group fingerprint to currentFingerprint() to warn, and to qualify the readiness text, when the judge no longer asks that question.

Upgrade

If you construct ResultsCompareController directly or subclass it, the new last constructor argument is optional (?PluginManagerInterface $graderManager = NULL). Without it, grader ids are shown as they are. Code or tests that match the old "(untagged)" failure-rate label must now expect "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" or "Deferred".

  • Committed: November 2, 2026

item.title: #3594861: Results screens show test, judge and gate metric ids instead of their names
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594861 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval results screens now show names instead of machine ids. The overview (Recent Runs, Target Health, pending optimizations), the result detail Run Summary and the compare warning show the test label, with the id in a title tooltip. The Judge trust badges show short judge names such as "Accuracy". The detail Gate cell shows "Pass rate" or "Average score" instead of pass_rate. The same 1.1.x commit also shipped several related results and calibration changes. The detail page and overview show the gate the run actually recorded, or "Gate not recorded" instead of an invented 4.0. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred". Annotate progress counts against the latest run's answers. Gate type wording now says that hard and soft only change the exit code of drush ai-eval:run. Calibration screens warn when saving replaced an inactive fit, or when the judge no longer asks the question a fit was made on. The compare page uses plain labels for differences and moves raw values into a closed "Technical details" section.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Results pages now render target names in a span or link with a title attribute holding the id, and the compare page has a new .ai-eval-readable-differences list plus a closed Technical details section.

Technical details

On the overview, EvalResultsController now loads the page's pending, latest and paged results first, then calls loadMultiple() once on ai_eval_target for all target ids. It uses those entities for the labels and adds ai_eval_target_list plus each target's cache tags to #cache. The detail page adds the same tags next to its existing max-age 0. When a target has been deleted, the id is shown as the text with no title. Judge badges pass graderShortLabel($id) as the text while the validation link keeps the real id. The compare page's different-test warning loads both targets and builds <span title="id">label</span> markup. ResultsCompareController gets an optional $graderManager constructor argument (ai_eval.grader_manager). It uses that argument to turn grader ids into plugin labels, and a differenceLabel() map to give difference keys plain names. Hashes show as "same", "changed" or "recorded", and raw values stay in the closed details element.

The new private recordedGate() resolves the gate from the result's validated config_json snapshot (metric and threshold). If the snapshot has no usable gate, it falls back to the live target's threshold. If neither exists it returns NULL, which gives "Gate not recorded" and drops the threshold from the Target Health score cell. The detail Gate cell prints GateMetric::label(). FailureRateService now groups by verdict as well as failure_mode. decorate() merges tagged verdicts back into one row per mode and splits only the rows without a mode by verdict, so the shares still sum to 100%. WorkflowStateService now reads question_count from the latest result and counts canonical annotations on it for Annotate progress. The suggested total of 100 is removed. A new GateTypeWording class supplies the gate type options and description for EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. CalibrationSaveTrait counts inactive curves for the same provider, model and fingerprint before saving and reports when one was replaced. CalibrationFromReviewsForm compares the group fingerprint with currentFingerprint() to warn about stale rubric wording. Docs and CHANGELOG are updated. The issue text proposes an EntityLabels::target() helper. The portion of the diff I could read does not add one, and the controllers call $target->label() directly.

item.title: #3594860: "Can fit: Yes" for reviewed answers the judge no longer asks about
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594860 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

This commit is a bundle of AI Eval 1.1.x UI fixes. The headline issue, #3594860, is the calibration "Fit from reviews" form. A reviewed group fitted on earlier rubric wording used to read a plain "Can fit: Yes", even though the judge would not apply that fit. The cell now says the judge does not ask this question now, and saving such a group shows a warning. The group stays selectable. The same commit also shows the gate a run actually used, or "Gate not recorded", instead of an invented 4.0. It shows test and grader names instead of ids on the results screens. The compare page uses plain-language differences. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into Passed, Failed with no failure mode, and Deferred. The Annotate progress bar counts the answers of the latest run. The hard and soft gate wording now says it only changes the exit code of drush ai-eval:run.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Calibration form: CalibrationFromReviewsForm::readinessText() compares the group's fingerprint with currentFingerprint() and, for a ready group that differs, returns "Yes, but the judge does not ask this question now, so it will not apply this fit". submitForm() adds a warning after a save when the fingerprint differs. The shared saveAndReport() is not changed for this. The warning text says the fit can apply again only if the rubric is restored, the fit is active, and it uses the judge's provider and model.

Gate shown for a run: EvalResultsController::recordedGate() reads the run's validated config snapshot (metric and threshold) first. It falls back to the live test's threshold, then to NULL. The results list and detail pages no longer default to 4.0. They show "Gate not recorded" on the detail page and omit the threshold comparison in the list. The metric is shown by label, for example "Pass rate", not pass_rate. The controller now loads the target entities once, shows the test label with the id as a title attribute, adds cache tags, and uses graderShortLabel() for judge trust badges. ResultsCompareController gets an optional ai_eval.grader_manager constructor argument. It maps snapshot keys to labels (differenceLabel()), shows hashes only as "same", "changed" or "recorded" (readableValue()), and moves raw key and value pairs into a closed "Technical details" element.

Failure rates and Annotate progress: FailureRateService now selects verdict as well. Rows with a failure mode merge back into one bucket per mode. Rows without a mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode", "Deferred" or "No verdict" (replacing (untagged)), so the shares still sum to 100%. Each row gains a verdict key. WorkflowStateService drops the fixed suggested total of 100 annotations. Progress is now the canonical annotation count on the latest result against that result's question_count, and the label is "N of M answers labeled". Gate wording is centralized in the new Drupal\ai_eval\Form\GateTypeWording, used by EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. A new message after saving a calibration says when it replaced earlier fits that were not active (#3594859). The commit also updates CHANGELOG.md and the user guides.

item.title: #3594859: Saving a calibration silently deletes the earlier fit that was not active
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594859 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

One commit in ai_eval 1.1.x fixes eight small UI problems found in a user-guide walkthrough, including #3594859. Saving a calibration now says when it replaced an earlier fit that was not active, because that fit is deleted. Results screens show the gate a run actually used, taken from the run's recorded settings. Runs with no recorded gate show "Gate not recorded" in place of an invented 4.0 threshold. Test names appear as labels instead of ids. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred". Annotate progress counts the answers of the latest run. The compare page uses plain labels for differences. The hard and soft gate options now say that the type only changes the exit code of drush ai-eval:run. A calibration whose question the decision rubric judge no longer asks now gets a warning that the judge will not apply it.

Impact

Affects front-end developers and site owners.

  • Config change: The gate type option labels in the target and guided test forms now describe the drush ai-eval:run exit code. The stored values hard and soft are unchanged.
  • Theme change: Failure-rate rows are labeled "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" or "Deferred" instead of "(untagged)". The results, compare and gate-type screens show different text and markup.

Technical details

The issue's fix is in CalibrationSaveTrait::saveAndReport(). It counts the pair's inactive curves via $this->store->curvesFor() before saving. After a successful save it adds a separate formatPlural() message ("It replaced the earlier fit that was not active." / "It replaced @count earlier fits that were not active."). The message is a warning when the new fit is inactive and a status message otherwise. CalibrationStore::replace() and the interface are unchanged. The count is read outside the store's lock, as the issue acknowledges.

The same commit covers the other items:

  • EvalResultsController::recordedGate() resolves the gate from the run's validated config snapshot (decodeValidatedSnapshot()), then falls back to the live target's threshold. If neither exists it returns NULL. The overview and detail pages then drop the threshold and verdict comparison, and the detail page shows "Gate not recorded". The metric is shown through GateMetric::label().
  • The results controller now loads the target entities once and adds their cache tags plus ai_eval_target_list. Target labels replace ids, with the id kept as a title attribute. Judge trust badges use graderShortLabel().
  • ResultsCompareController gets an optional graderManager constructor argument (ai_eval.grader_manager). It adds differenceLabel() and readableValue(), so hashes show as "same", "changed" or "recorded" and grader ids show as labels. Raw values move into a closed "Technical details" details element.
  • FailureRateService now also groups by verdict. Rows with no failure mode are labeled by verdict, tagged verdicts are merged back into their mode, and the rates still sum to 1. Each row gains a verdict key.
  • WorkflowStateService computes Annotate progress as canonical annotations on the latest result against its question_count. The fixed suggested total of 100 is removed.
  • GateTypeWording is a new helper shared by EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. It supplies the gate option labels, a description and the review text.
  • CalibrationFromReviewsForm compares the group's fingerprint with currentFingerprint() to show the warning and a "Yes, but the judge does not ask this question now..." readiness text.
  • The docs and CHANGELOG are updated to match.

item.title: #3594858: Failure rates table counts passed answers under "(untagged)"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594858 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The failure-rates table in AI Eval used one "(untagged)" row for every answer with no failure mode. That row included passed answers, so "(untagged) 60%" looked like 60% of answers had failed in an unnamed way. That row is now split by verdict into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred". The labels are translatable, rows with a zero count are hidden, and the rows still add up to 100%. Rows for named failure modes are unchanged. The same commit also ships several other 1.1.x results and calibration changes, listed in the changelog, such as the recorded gate on results screens, plain compare-page labels and Annotate progress counted against the latest run.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: FailureRateService rate rows gain a verdict key. Rows with no failure mode are now split into three rows, so code that keys rows by failure_mode alone must account for it. Their label changes from (untagged) to "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" or "Deferred".

Technical details

FailureRateService::aggregate() now selects and groups by verdict as well as failure_mode. decorate() then folds tagged rows back into one bucket per mode, so mode rows keep their old counts. Rows with no mode are bucketed per verdict. The denominator is unchanged, which keeps the sum at 100%. ratesForReviewedTraces() also selects verdict from ai_eval_review_label and keeps it beside the mode for the earliest label per trace_key. Both paths go through decorate().

Each rate row gains a verdict key. It is NULL for rows that carry a mode and one of pass, fail or defer for the no-mode rows. For those rows failure_mode stays NULL and label comes from TranslatableMarkup: "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" or "Deferred". A fallback "No verdict" label covers any other value. Callers that index rows by failure_mode alone can no longer tell the three no-mode rows apart and need to check verdict. The FailureRateTable docblock was updated, and the render code needed no change. docs/user/usage/failure-modes.md and the changelog describe the new rows.

Upgrade

Code that reads FailureRateService rows and looks for the (untagged) label, or indexes rows by failure_mode alone, should use the new verdict key to tell the three no-mode rows apart. Rows with a mode have verdict set to NULL.

item.title: #3594857: Annotate step shows "0 of 100 suggested" for a test that has 8 answers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +912/−168 · php +893/−159 · md +19/−9
  • Diff: c561855
  • Discussion: #3594857 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Annotate step (step 2 of the error-analysis workflow) used to show progress against a fixed target of 100, so a test with 8 answers read "0 of 100 suggested" even after every answer was labeled. It now counts labeled answers on the latest run and reads, for example, "12 of 20 answers labeled". Step 2 is Done only when the latest run is fully labeled, so running the test again takes it back to "Start here". Deferred answers count as labeled. The same commit also changes several related screens in ai_eval (1.1.x). Results screens show the gate a run actually used, or "Gate not recorded", instead of an invented 4.0 threshold, and they show test names instead of ids. Failure-rate rows without a failure mode are split into "Passed", "Failed, no failure mode" and "Deferred". The compare page uses plain labels. Gate type wording now says it only changes the exit code of drush ai-eval:run. Calibration screens warn when a fit will not apply because the rubric wording changed, and when a saved fit replaced an inactive one.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The annotate step's progress array from WorkflowStateService no longer has a suggested key, and progress is NULL when the latest result has no questions. FailureRateService rows gain a verdict key and the (untagged) label is replaced.

Technical details

Annotate progress: WorkflowStateService drops ANNOTATION_TARGET and the suggested flag. latestResult() now also selects question_count. done is the number of canonical annotations (via AnnotationStore::joinCanonical()) on the latest result's result_id, and total is its question_count. The target-wide $labeled count is kept for the grouping floor, rates and promote steps. item.title: #3586825: Forward/Backward-Port: Add automator ID tag and entity_context to chat requests (1.4.x & 2.0.x)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 28 files, +2871/−10 · php +2685/−10 · md +186
  • Diff: cbe279c
  • Discussion: #3586825 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

Chat requests that AI Automators send to a provider now identify which automator made them. Each request gets an ai_automator:id:{config entity ID} tag and an entity_context metadata array describing the entity and field. Several automators on the same field (for example separate Field Widget Action buttons) previously produced requests with identical tags, so event subscribers could not tell them apart. This was ported to 2.0.x/2.x and backported to 1.4.x after landing on 1.x and 1.5.x (#3586702).

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: On 1.4.x the InputBase request metadata methods (getAllRequestMetadata(), setAllRequestMetadata(), getRequestMetadataValue(), setRequestMetadataValue()) are added, and ProviderProxy seeds pre and post event metadata from the input. Code that rebuilds the automator config array in AutomatorConfigEvent subscribers on 1.4.x must keep the id key.
  • New API: Automator chat requests carry a new ai_automator:id:{automator config entity ID} tag and entity_context request metadata (entity_type, entity_id, uuid, bundle, field_name, automator_id). New protected RuleBase::buildEntityContext() and RuleBase::attachEntityContext() helpers.

Technical details

RuleBase::getTags() now adds ai_automator:id:{id} when the automator config carries a string ID. RuleBase::runRawChatMessage() and the rich-text image description path in RichTextImageDescriptionTrait call the new attachEntityContext() on the final input, after applyGuardrailsToInput(), because that helper can return a clone. buildEntityContext() returns entity_type, entity_id, uuid, bundle, field_name and automator_id. entity_id is NULL for new (unsaved) entities, so presave requests are identified by uuid. The metadata is read with $event->getMetadata('entity_context'). Rules that build their own ChatInput (Chart, VideoToText, LlmVideo*, Field Widget Action refine chat) still send untagged requests, as the added docs state.

On 2.0.x/2.x the automator ID, field name and plugin ID are not stored settings. AiAutomatorEntityModifier::withRuntimeContext() clones each automator type and adds automator_id, field_name and rule to its settings, so nothing leaks into exported config. These runtime settings are set after the stored ones, so a stray stored setting with the same key cannot override them. RunAutomatorAction sets the same three keys, and the tag and metadata read automator_id.

On 1.4.x the ID lives in the id key of the runtime automator config instead. AiAutomatorEntityModifier::entityHasConfig() and RunAutomatorAction set it from the config entity ID, after the plugin_config keys are unprefixed. RuleBase::attachEntityContext() there is guarded with method_exists($input, 'setRequestMetadataValue'). The 1.4.x commit also adds request metadata to InputBase. ProviderProxy seeds the PreGenerateResponseEvent metadata from the input and passes the post event metadata to streamed responses. It also re-applies the input's system prompt to the provider after the pre-generate event, so event subscribers can change it.

Upgrade

Subscribers can target one automator by tag:

public function onPreGenerate(PreGenerateResponseEvent $event): void {
  if (!in_array('ai_automator:id:node.article.field_summary.default', $event->getTags(), TRUE)) {
    return;
  }
  $context = $event->getMetadata('entity_context');
  // $context['entity_id'] is NULL on presave; fall back to uuid or bundle.
}

Custom rules that build their own ChatInput should call $this->attachEntityContext($input, $entity, $automatorConfig); and pass $this->getTags(...) to chat(). On 2.x, code calling a rule outside AiAutomatorEntityModifier or RunAutomatorAction must add automator_id, field_name and rule to the settings itself. On 1.4.x, AutomatorConfigEvent subscribers that rebuild the config array must keep its id key, or the ID tag and automator_id are dropped.

The button fetches a blank input from the new RubricController::phraseRow() route ai_eval.rubric.phrase_row. item.title: #3594851: Say so when no chat provider is set up, instead of a blank Provider / Model text box
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 58 files, +1118/−90 · php +1011/−89 · js +77 · yml +16 · md +14/−1
  • Diff: 499dc1e
  • Discussion: #3594851 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In AI Eval, the guided test form and the classic test target form now say so when the AI module lists no chat models. Before, both showed a bare "Provider / Model" text box. The format only appeared in an error after submit. Now a warning says no chat models are available and that one possible cause is a missing provider or key. Users with the administer ai providers permission get a link to the AI provider settings. Other users are told to ask an administrator. The text field stays as a fallback, with a description that says to type provider__model, for example openai__gpt-4o-mini. When models are listed, the select and its description are unchanged. The same commit also bundles several unrelated fixes, such as singular and plural wording, named row buttons, and Enter no longer saving a rubric.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ProviderModelOptionsTrait gains noChatModelsNotice() and manualModelDescription(), now also used by GuidedTestForm and EvalTargetForm.

Technical details

GuidedTestForm and EvalTargetForm now use ProviderModelOptionsTrait::providerModelOptions() in place of their own try/catch blocks. Because of this, the guided form now reports a load failure as a warning with the exception message and a log entry, as the classic form already did. The trait tracks providerModelLoadFailed. noChatModelsNotice() returns a render element that is hidden (#access) when the failure message was already shown, so the user does not see two warnings. It checks administer ai providers to decide whether to render a Link to ai.admin_providers. It adds the user.permissions cache context. manualModelDescription() supplies the text field description. The classic form keeps its original select description only when options exist. The provider__model validation after submit is unchanged.

New tests are NoChatModelsTest, which covers the link with and without the permission and the format error on submit, and ChatModelsAvailableTest, which uses the ai_test provider to check that the select and old description are kept.
